questions: Can I start Unity without knowing C#?
Yes. We begin with the editor and simple game actions, then introduce C# variables, conditions, loops and methods through the project. The aim is to understand the code, not just run it.
Can I bring an existing game?
Yes. We look at the project and choose a manageable next step. Complex games take time, so I do not promise completion in a fixed number of lessons.

courses.title: Learn Python through Minecraft — online lessons
courses.heading: Python foundations through Minecraft
courses.description: Individual Python lessons through Minecraft with course author Sivochka Ihor. Learn coordinates, loops, conditions and building with code online.
courses.intro: Minecraft becomes a place to experiment with Python: write commands and see the game world change. I developed a course on programming foundations through Minecraft; I now use Minescript for lessons.
topics: Player and block coordinates
Python variables, conditions, loops and functions
Automating repeated actions in the game
Debugging and checking results in Minecraft
examples: Teleport the player to random coordinates
Build a fortress or lay rails with code
Check blocks below the player and react to lava
steps: Check the Minecraft version, Minescript setup and Zoom screen sharing. A computer is required; we discuss the setup before the lesson.
Start with coordinates and short commands, connecting changes in the game to Python concepts.
Combine commands into a program, adding conditions, loops and individual rules at a suitable pace.
questions: Is Minecraft on a tablet enough?
This direction needs a computer with Minecraft, a compatible Minescript setup and Zoom screen sharing. We check the game version and installation options before starting.
How is this different from simply playing?
Students write Python, predict the result and test it in Minecraft. The game makes coordinates, conditions and loops visible; understanding programming is the goal.

minecraft_evidence.title: The course behind my Minecraft lessons
minecraft_evidence.text: In 2021 I received second place in the All-Ukrainian student research competition in Secondary Education (Computer Science). My work explored teaching programming foundations through Minecraft. Tasks included teleportation, building a fortress and laying rails with code.
minecraft_evidence.note: The public materials from that course use mcpi. They are historical examples; current Minescript lessons require a different setup.
